title: Messaging Convergence Guide — MLE / Backend / Platform
content:
Purpose:
Short working brief to align on differentiated messaging for three adjacent engineering personas: ML engineers (MLEs), backend engineers, and platform teams. This is intentionally tactical — pick 2–3 claims per persona we can test in outreach and product pages.

Summary / thesis:
- Common problem across personas: inference is where product risk (latency, cost, reliability) shows up. But each persona cares about different levers, language, and proof.
- Goal: create convergent core narrative (Unified serving, predictable economics, safe fallbacks) and persona-specific hooks/proofs that map to their day-to-day KPIs.

Persona briefs (working):
1) ML engineers (MLEs) — profile:
- Primary goals: model fidelity, reproducible evaluation, easy iteration with fast feedback loops.
- Day-to-day pain: production mismatch (dev vs prod model performance), token cost surprises, and slow experiment-to-prod path.
- What they respond to: quality-first performance claims, evals/benchmarks, prompt-level regression alerts, infer-accurate SDKs.
- Top messages to test: 
  * "Ship models without the last-mile performance surprises" — highlight eval-integrated rollouts and regression alerts.
  * "Preserve model quality while cutting cost" — quantify quality-preserving quantization & model-variant fallbacks.
- Proof points to surface: per-prompt regression history, A/B eval harnesses, fidelity-preserving quantization case study (customer X reduced cost 3x with <1% BLEU/ROUGE drop).

2) Backend engineers — profile:
- Primary goals: reliable low-latency endpoints, predictable cost, simple integration.
- Day-to-day pain: high tail latency, expensive autoscaling, complex ops surface for batching/caching.
- What they respond to: SLA demos, latency percentiles, SDKs (Java/Go), simple routing policies.
- Top messages to test: 
  * "Predictable latency at scale" — emphasize 99th percentile numbers, burst handling, and automatic fallbacks.
  * "Integrates like a normal API" — show SDK examples, request/response samples, observability hooks.
- Proof points to surface: 99.9% uptime SLA, 50ms median / 180ms p99 on typical customer traffic, plug-and-play SDK snippets.

3) Platform teams — profile:
- Primary goals: standardization, security/compliance, cost allocation and multi-tenant efficiency.
- Day-to-day pain: divergent teams re-inventing inference, chargeback complexity, audit/compliance gaps.
- What they respond to: compatibility with KMS/VPC, private deployments, RBAC, rollout controls, cost optimization tools.
- Top messages to test: 
  * "One inference platform across hosted / dedicated / private" — emphasize consistent APIs and policy controls.
  * "Move from stove-piped endpoints to governed capacity" — show autoscale policies, chargeback dashboards.
- Proof points to surface: private deployment reference (regulated customer Y), KMS/HSM integration checklist, cost-savings after dedup of teams.

Competitive analysis notes (high level):
- Large hosted API providers (X): appeal to product teams and quick prototyping. Gap: limited private deployment controls and limited rollout primitives. Messaging: emphasize Redwood Private + rollout fidelity.
- Inference runtimes / vendors (Y): focus on kernel-level optimizations and self-host flexibility. Gap: lacks unified telemetry and easy multi-tenant control plane. Messaging: emphasize Redwood’s combined runtime + control plane.
- Open-source/self-host path: attractive for cost but heavy ops. Messaging: call out TCO (ops + engineering hours) and show comparison matrix for 6/12/24 month horizon.
- Niche competitors (replicate-style): easy sharing but limited production SLAs and no integrated chargeback. Messaging: point to SLA + observability + cost controls.

Positioning drafts (short):
- Core headline (shared): "Predictable, production-grade inference — anywhere you run it."
- MLE variant: "Ship models with the same quality you validated locally — and get automatic regression alerts if it changes."
- Backend variant: "APIs that behave like your other services — low p99, built-in fallbacks, and straightforward SDKs."
- Platform variant: "A single platform for inference governance — private deployments, chargeback, and rollout policy controls."

Talk tracks / outreach snippets (quick, testable):
- Cold email line for MLEs: "Tired of 'works-in-notebook' but fails at scale? Our eval-integrated rollouts catch regressions before customers do."
- Cold email for backend: "Can we show you a 5-minute demo of p99 improvements and simpler autoscale for model endpoints?"
- SDR/AE demo hook for platform: "We consolidated inference for a 200-engineer org and cut duplicated spend by 36% — want the model for your org?"

Objection handling (concise):
- "We can just self-host/open-source": acknowledge tech maturity but ask about SLOs, ongoing ops cost, and multi-team governance. Offer TCO worksheet.
- "We already have a vendor": ask which gaps they still see (rollouts, private deployment, cost controls) and offer a short audit.
- "Latency/cost tradeoff concerns": show case study with quantization + KV cache savings and no measurable regression.

Metrics & artifacts to surface on page/demo:
- p50 / p95 / p99 numbers on reference workloads, per-token cost comparisons across model variants, time-to-rollout (canary -> full), incident history for fallbacks.
- Live demo scripts: (1) show prompt regression alert, (2) perform canary rollback, (3) show chargeback dashboard by team.

Unresolved questions / research needed (action items):
- Need 2 MLE-facing case studies where model quality was preserved while cutting cost via quantization. (Owner: Priya)
- Obtain p99 latency traces for 3 representative customers for demo (Owner: Ethan / SRE).
- Draft TCO calculator for 6/12/24 months vs self-hosted (Owner: Lucas).
- Legal/Privacy checklist for Private deployment one-pager (ask security team).

Next steps (this doc's cadence):
- Iterate with product on exact numbers we can expose publicly (by 2025-12-10).
- Build 3 outbound templates (MLE / backend / platform) and A/B test subject lines and first-sentence claims.
- Design landing page variants that keep core headline but rotate persona proofs.

Notes to self / rough reminders: 
- Keep MLE messaging tied to quantifiable evals — vague "better quality" language won’t convert.
- Backend demos should be <7 minutes and include p99 numbers + SDK snippet in the first 90s.
- Platform buyers care deeply about integrations (KMS, AD, VPC) — surface those logos/checkboxes.
